correctness.rationale: The exact Euclidean disk inequalities reduce, quadrant by quadrant, to one upper and one lower radial threshold. The angular interval has a forbidden set precisely when 2u²−tu+1≤0, yielding 4 components for t<√8 and 8 for t≥√8, with endpoint explicitly handled. The polar integral has explicit primitive G_t, and the local double-root expansion gives the 3/2-power correction with coefficient 2·2^(1/4)/9. Standalone checker directly compares original four disk membership against polar integral and verifies rational identities. Numerical finite tests support, but only the analytic proof covers all real t≥1.

value.rationale: The exact count-one locus measures nonredundant coverage, unlike a power-diagram partition; rectangles are the full natural one-parameter family of four-vertex orthogonal boxes in the plane. Its sharp threshold is accompanied by topological change and a fractional-power onset in an area invariant. The finding is a full classification along a mathematically motivated family, not a mere t=1 regular-polygon special case.
